card: Prevents premature chain sync eviction of outbound peers during anti-DoS headers presync. When syncing headers below minimum chain work, headers are held in presync and not stored in the block index, leaving the peer's best known block null. On high-latency connections like Tor or I2P, the 22-minute chain sync timeout can expire before mainnet's ~480 presync round trips finish, disconnecting the peer and discarding presync progress. The patch factors work accumulated during presync into eviction checks, accompanied by a functional test reproducing the timeout on master.
evidence: PR description explains the interaction gap: chain sync eviction from #11490 was never integrated with headers presync introduced in #25717.

PR author includes a reproduction test where an outbound peer sending one header batch per mocked minute is disconnected on master after 24 minutes with 'Outbound peer has old chain', but remains connected with the fix.
problem: When a node's best header is below minimum chain work, incoming headers are held in an anti-DoS presync phase without being committed to the block index, leaving the peer's best known block pointer null. As a result, chain sync eviction logic treats the peer as unresponsive and disconnects it after roughly 22 minutes, terminating headers sync and wiping presync progress for users on slow or high-latency connections like Tor or I2P.

risk.why: A mistake in peer eviction logic could cause nodes to stay connected to stalled or hostile peers instead of evicting them to find responsive sync partners.

summary: Counts accumulated chainwork during anti-DoS headers presync when checking outbound peers for chain sync eviction in net_processing. Peers delivering headers during presync are treated as caught up if their presync work meets or exceeds the local node's tip work, preventing premature disconnection.
